title: Longest Subarray with At Most K Distinct Values
statement: You are given a list of integers nums and an integer k (k >= 1). A subarray is a contiguous slice of nums. Return the length of the longest subarray that contains at most k distinct values. If nums is empty, return 0. The result is a single non-negative integer, uniquely determined: you want the maximum possible window length, not the window itself, so ties among equally long windows do not matter.
reference_solution:
def longest_subarray_k_distinct(nums, k):
    from collections import defaultdict
    counts = defaultdict(int)
    left = 0
    best = 0
    for right, v in enumerate(nums):
        counts[v] += 1
        while len(counts) > k:
            counts[nums[left]] -= 1
            if counts[nums[left]] == 0:
                del counts[nums[left]]
            left += 1
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best
hints: You want the longest contiguous run whose variety of values stays within a limit — brute forcing every start and end recomputes overlapping ranges, so what work could you carry from one candidate range to the next?
Track the values currently inside the window with a frequency map; the number of distinct values is exactly how many keys the map holds.

Extend right by one each step, incrementing that value's count. While the map has more than k keys, decrement nums[left] and, crucially, delete the key when its count reaches zero so the distinct count actually drops; then move left forward. Record right - left + 1 as a candidate best.
